data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The advantage of the bounded harness is purely statistical: it increases the number of independent samples (N) drawn from the model's distribution, making the maximum quality of the set max(C_1...C_N) strictly greater than or equal to a single sample C_1, regardless of any 'selection' logic.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the model's outputs are highly autocorrelated across calls (lack of diversity), increasing N does not significantly expand the covered search space.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the cost of generation scales linearly with N but the quality gain diminishes logarithmically, the efficiency ratio may favor a single, highly prompted call.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 'harness' actively modifies the generation process (e.g., via context updates), the samples are no longer independent, complicating the statistical argument.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Extreme value theory application: Assuming the model has a non-zero probability of generating a valid conjecture, running the model N times (even with a dumb harness that just collects all outputs) increases the likelihood of hitting the tail of the quality distribution. The 'survival' aspect is merely the observation of this maximum.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
